DEVICES_RESULT: The four device packages were assembled from this tree by `tools/device_package.py` and run with the publishers' figures on 2026-10-23, each in its own process. Each first checked the tested versions, the code stamp and the sha256 of every input, then built its photomasks, registered them on the papers' micrographs and rendered the overlays, and every one ended its last step. All 11 photomasks are byte-identical to the release's, which are RC8's. Per package: `gifford2014_fig6` (43 min): two photomasks byte-identical, four registration records equal to RC8's in every value, 20 measurements within their regression limits; `gifford2014_fig4` (37 min): five photomasks byte-identical, five registration records equal to RC8's in every value, every result of the taper-direction test (V13) equal to RC8's, with the nested reading's neighbouring leg PASS, reading B's FAIL and every leg-4 control PASS, the claim's leg on the inset within its regression limits; `dinh2024_v1` (21 min): two photomasks byte-identical, two registration records equal to RC8's in every value; `xia2016_rs7` (54 min): two photomasks byte-identical, 12 registration records equal to RC8's in every value. The packages' outputs, which embed the publishers' figures, are among the release's evidence assets rather than in this repository. The first run of the Xia package stopped at its trace step on an error of the restructure in five trace scripts, which was corrected (CHANGELOG item 14) before all four packages were run again; the results above are from that second run. After it, the kits' source notes (`inputs/SOURCE.md`) were updated to say that the figures are distributed in `notebooks/figures/`, which changed the sha256 of each kit's source note in its `MANIFEST.json` and `reference/EXPECT.json` and no other entry, and each kit then assembled from the published tree with the figures of `notebooks/figures/` and passed its check step.
TUTORIAL_RESULT: The tutorial (`notebooks/opencif_tutorial.ipynb`) was executed in full (`QUICK = False`) on this tree with the tested versions in 50 min, and none of its 37 code cells is in error. The published notebook is that executed one, with the text of its section 12 updated afterwards to say that the figures are distributed (no code cell or output changed), and it contains no absolute path of the machine that ran it. Its section 6 built a new device from D = 4 µm and F = 0.5 (verdict PASS, exit 0, physics audit PASS). Its section 7.1 audited that photomask again from scratch, and the audit gave PASS, with every check's verdict equal to that of the build's own audit (the checks whose recorded value differs in its last digits or in the row where it peaks: R0, P2, P4, P5). Its section 10 rebuilt the four published devices, and every photomask is byte-identical to the release's.
REVIEW_RESULT: Two reviewers worked independently on the tree as published and on the build's evidence (2026-10-23): one on the physics, the drawing and its measurement, and the gates, and the other on reproducibility, the documents against the records, the tutorial, and the repository's hygiene. Both found the physics sound. Every finding was checked against the code or the records before it was acted on. The release keeps its code stamp, because its photomasks, records and audits were built and validated at that stamp, so a finding about the package is answered by documents that say what the code does, and the code change is listed for the next release (`docs/LIMITATIONS.md` item 31). The documents, the tests' workflow, the tools outside the package and the provenance were corrected where needed (CHANGELOG item 14). A third reviewer re-audited every row of `docs/ALIGNMENT.md` against `foundation/` and the restructured code (criterion 5 of `docs/EVALUATION.md` section 8). It found one row to relabel, AA16, whose floor start departed from spec v5 §10 and M6 (row S3, erratum D108), and ten smaller corrections; after they were made, its re-check found every row correctly labelled. At the author's direction the specification was then corrected in place (revision 5.1, `foundation/README.md`). The two suites that read the documents were run again after every change, with identical logs. The reviews and the record of what was done with each finding are among the release's evidence assets. With these, the release meets the six criteria of `docs/EVALUATION.md` section 8: sections 1 to 3 of this page and `docs/RESULTS.md` show criteria 1 to 4, the re-audit shows criterion 5, and for criterion 6 the commands of its sections 4 and 5 were run as printed: the rebuilt `gifford2014_fig4_design` and `m11_paperclip_const_pack_filter_ring` equal their records in every compared field (the verdict, the realised cutoff, the network, the physics audit, every check's value, and the photomask's sha256), and the new design passes and the three refusals refuse for the reasons printed (the comments on two of them were corrected to name the refusal on w_min at row 1 that comes first).
